description.JP: This is a special Time Trial event for the Gran Turismo Series 15th anniversary cars. If the starting PP of your car is well below the 631 PP limit of the entry rule, you may find it difficult to achieve the target time even if you adjust its settings. Hit your best laptime to gain the Gold prize!

description.JP: This is a time trial for Honda's only front engine/rear wheel drive car, the S2000. It is possible to acquire the S2000 by clearing the National A Class License test. A special prize is also awarded with a Gold result. Rear wheel drives like the S2000 require careful throttle control. Flooring the pedal can upset the orientation of your car, so make sure to press the accelerator gradually to prevent the rear wheels from sliding out.

To achieve a good laptime in this stage, it is important to utilize the width of the track effectively to raise your average speed. Use the full width all way up to the gravel!

A Special prize is also awarded for achieving the Gold result in this event. The X-Bow with its excellent turn-in characteristics requires the driver to avoid oversteering, that will disrupt the car's balance.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using the XKR-S, the car often referred to as Jaguars' ultimate sports coupe. The Jaguar XKR-S can also be acquired by achieving half the stars in the International B Class. Although the car is powerful to begin with, this track often requires full acceleration, and if you're going to tune the car, increased power is the way to go. If you want to rely more on cornering, weight reduction and suspension upgrades are a must.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using Toyota's popular FR sports model, the 86GT. The event is also open to the Anniversary edition of the 86GT. While increasing the power of the engine is effective, be careful that you don't upset the balance and make the car difficult to control. In addition, as this is a technical course, it may be prudent to practice the track until you are more familiar with it rather then tuning your car right off the bat. Don't forget to always use the full width of the track!

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using the High End Performance G37, the car which won the "Gran Turismo Awards SEMA" at the 2008 SEMA show. The car can be acquired by clearing the International A License with all gold results. Because the stage is a technical circuit, weight reductions will be more effective than power tuning in this Time Trial.

This car can be acquired by clearing the Goodwood FoS in all Gold results after receiving the first invitation. Because its gear ratios are too short for the course, we recommend changing the transmission first when you tune the car.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using the racing version of the Lotus Elise. The event can be entered using the Elise Race Car '96 that can be acquired by achieving all Gold results in the International B Class mission races, or with the Elise 111R Race Car '04. Both have strong oversteer characteristics; if you find it difficult to drive, you can reduce the downforce in front of the car, or increase the downforce in the back, adjusting the front/rear balance to your preference. It will be important to understand the base characteristics of the car and adjust accordingly, rather than tuning the car arbitrarily.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using the racing version of the Diablo that was developed for the FIA-GT Championships. This car can be purchased at the car dealership or acquired by completing the International B Class license with all stars. Understeer will be a problem in the mid to high speed corners and can be alleviated by reducing weight in tuning. This track has a relatively long flat out section, so more power for the engine will also prove effective.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using the Plymouth XNR Ghia Roadster, the car that was awarded the "Gran Turismo Trophy" at the 2011 Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance. You can acquire this car by purchasing it or by clearing the "Goodwood Festival of Speed" event thet opens with the second invitation with all Gold results. The car only has 3 gears to begin with, so the recommended first step in tuning is to replace the transmission. To aim for a Gold result, use the full width of the track and try to maintain your speed as much as possible.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event on the Tsukuba Circuit, in wet surface conditions after rain. The event can be challenged with the EV convertible sportscar of Tesla Motors, the Tesla Roadster. Early braking and careful throttle work are required due to the slippery surface conditions. You'll produce better results if you prevent the car from sliding sideways as much as possible!

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using Mazda's famous lightweight FR sportscar, the Eunos Roadster/MX-5/Miata. Because this track has a long full-throttle section, it will be effective to start by tuning the engine power first. You'll still be underpowered compared to cars with bigger engines, so drive effectively and set the car to maximise the power available. Take on the challenge by personalising the Roadster to fit your driving style.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using the Clio R.S. '11, a hot hatch created by the motorsports department of the manufacturer Renault, "Renault Sport". This car can be purchased in the car dealership or acquired by completing all stars in the Novice class. The trick to shortening your time is in your racing lines, rather than tuning. You must make sure to clip the inside on the first corner, and on the exit of the last corner, try to turn your car's heading as early as possible to allow full throttle. Use the full width of the wide track effectively for the best result.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial Event using a racing model developed by Ferrari solely for circuit use, the Ferrari FXX. An event courtesy car will be provided so anyone can participate in the event. The key to shortening laptimes lies in how you handle the three chicanes. Rather than braking as late as possible, you should focus on braking early and place more emphasis on accelerating out of the corner.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using a car with fanatical fans all over the world; the Impreza (non-racing car) 4WD sportscar. It's up to the driver to chose between tuning overall performance of the car by reducing weight, or to increase power for the steep ascent in the latter half of the track. Road holding characteristics will also be important here, and we recommend tuning the suspension to match. There are numerous points on this track where the car can lose control, even rolling on its side in some cases. Drive with caution!

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using the BMW Concept 1 Series tii. This car can be acquired in the Car Dealership or by clearing the National A Class Mission Races with all Gold results. The stage is set in the Madrid City course which combines mid to low speed corners with a flat out section. To be quick on this course you should focus on tuning the car to turn and accelerate quickly. For the best results, make sure to fine tune your drivetrain starting from your transmission, rather than just increasing your car's overall PP.

To be quick on this course you should focus on tuning the car to turn and accelerate quickly. For the best results, make sure to fine tune your drivetrain starting from your transmission, rather than just increasing your car's overall PP.

description.JP:
This is a special event commemorating the presentation of the Toyota FT-1 at the New York International Auto Show. Achieve Bronze or better results in a Time Trial on the Fuji Speedway GT, and you will be awarded an FT-1 you can use in the game!
In addition, we are also hosting a special event using the "Photo Travel" mode. For details please refer to the official Gran Turismo website at http://www.gran-turismo.com/

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using the E-RUNNER Pikes Peak Special, the EV racing car that was brought to the 2012 Pikes Peak Hill Climb by Nobuhiro "Monster" Tajima. A courtesy car is provided to allow anyone to participate in the event. To aim for the Gold Prize, you'll need to effectively utilize the huge torque of the EV by fully reducing your speed where you need to, and giving it full throttle as necessary, all the while making sure not to slide the car around as much as you can.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using the ever popular Mazda RX-7 (FD) non-racing car. The event is geared for mid to expert level drivers with Skid Recovery turned OFF. We recommend tuning the car for high top speed to match the long straightaway. The other key is to find a setting that can handle mid to high speed corners well. Hardening the suspension will stabilize the car to a certain point, but keep in mind that making it too hard will increase understeer.

description.JP: This is a beginner to mid level Time Trial Event with the Skid Recovery Force turned ON. Because this is an urban course with tight corners, we recommend tuning your car for quicker acceleration. This can be done by replacing the transmission to shorten your gear ratios (reducing top speed), but installation of an LSD and reinforcing your clutch and flywheel is also recommended. The other trick to achieving a good time here is to boldly utilize the full width of the course when setting up your racing line, all the way up to the walls.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using the GT350, a hot model tuned by Carol Shelby for racing based on the Mustang Fastback. A courtesy car is provided so that you can participate in the event without owning the car. With a great balanced chassis, its handling is quick, but you still have to be careful as turning the steering wheel too much will result in oversteer of the car. Because of the powerful engine, you'll also have to be careful on the throttle. The trick to attaining the best times is to control your throttle carefully to avoid that oversteer.

With a great balanced chassis, its handling is quick, but you still have to be careful as turning the steering wheel too much will result in oversteer of the car. Because of the powerful engine, you'll also have to be careful on the throttle. The trick to attaining the best times is to control your throttle carefully to avoid that oversteer.

description.JP: This is a Mid to Expert level Time Trial event using one of the leading Japanese Sportscars, the Nissan Skyline GT-R. Skid Recovery Force is turned OFF in this event. As long as it is a non-racecar, any model from the R32/R33/R34 can be selected. The GT-R is a powerful and stable car, but in technical tracks with repetitive tight corners, its weight can be an issue. Turning and acceleration are the key points on this track, so the first step you may want to take in tuning is weight reduction. If you want to change the steering characteristics, it will be more effective to adjust the drive distribution rather than changing the suspension settings. The car will tend to stabilize more and understeer as you allocate more drive force to the front wheels.

description.JP: This is a beginner to mid level Time Trial event using Land Rover's cross over SUV, the Range Rover Evoke Coupe Dynamic. Skid recovery is ON in this event. This car can be acquired in the car dealership, or by clearing the International A class license. Weight reduction is definitely recommended when tuning, but more engine power is also good for the climb in the mid section of the track. There are many tight corners, making traction during acceleration very important, and will require the driver to avoid drifting the car as much as possible.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using the Huayra '13, an award winning supercar that replaced the Pagani Zonda. A courtesy car is provided so you don't need to own one to participate in this event. The first hurdle in combining an urban track and a fast car is trying to run a clear lap without hitting the walls. Time trials often require you to use the full width of the track, but to secure a valid time you'll need to hold back. Also, be careful not to drive over the inside cornerstones too much, as it can upset your balance while cornering.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial Event for Expert level drivers using the Suzuki Cappuccino, a popular compact FR sportscar with great driving performance. Skid recovery is turned OFF in this event. Because its power is fairly subtle, we would recommend tuning for more power output to begin. It will also be effective to fine tune the drive train as well as suspension, as these will not affect your performance points. The short wheel base makes the car naturally prone to oversteer, so the key to driving and tuning will be in how to suppress this behavior.

description.JP: This is a beginner to mid level Time Trial event using the Renault Sport Mégane R.S. Trophy, the high performance model of Renault Sport with high grip tires and 19 inch wheels. Skid Recovery Force is turned ON in this event. We recommend tuning your car to increase power in anticipation for the long full throttle sections, but to achieve the best lap times you'll need to do more than just go fast in a straight line. Rather than delaying your braking to the last moment, in general it will be better to focus on exit speed by completing braking early on and switching as soon as possible to acceleration.

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event on the Daytona Road Course, using a standard non-racing Chevrolet Corvette. Though the drivetrain is suited for drifting, handling the huge power output of the Corvette will not be easy. If you find it too hard to control, you may want to hold down the engine power using the restrictor feature. To attain high scores, you'll need to drift as long as possible from high speeds. Aim for the gold prize by balancing throttle and steering control!

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial Event using the Silvia, the front engine rear wheel drive sports car of Nissan that was popular among young drivers of its day. The stage is set on the Suzuka Circuit East course. The year model is not restricted, and only non-racing cars are allowed in the event. The Silvia is a car that is relatively easy to drift due to its front engine rear wheel drive layout and its excellent chassis balance. However the engine power is relatively low in its stock state, so the first thing you'll want to do is raise its power. The trick to gaining high scores is to enter the first section at the highest possible speed, and to maintain your drift during the 2nd and 3rd sections where you need to change direction. Be especially careful for the 4th section, it is easy to spin out during the descent in the latter half!

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial Event on the High Speed Ring/Reverse, using only four wheel drive (4WD) non-racing cars. 4WD cars are extremely stable, which means that drive train tuning and settings are mandatory to make them suitable for drifting. One major point in tuning is the distribution of drive force. If you install a center differential and set the drive force stronger on the rear tires, the car can be made to oversteer on throttle application so that it will be easier to drift.

If you install a center differential and set the drive force stronger on the rear tires, the car can be made to oversteer on throttle application so that it will be easier to drift.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using two popular front engine rear wheel drive sportscars, the Toyota 86 and the Subaru BRZ co-developed by Toyota and Subaru. Tuning is allowed up to 480PP, making it possible to fully tune the car, but what will make the real difference in time will be how you set the suspension and drive train. Brands Hatch is a course with a lot of mid to high speed corners, so it will be important to try to find a setting that stabilizes the car in those speed ranges. Aerodynamic parts that improve downforce is especially recommended.

description.JP: This is a time trial event using front wheel drive non-racing cars with 400PP or less. The Eiger Nordwand short course is a technical track with tight repetitive corners, which means that compact cars with a short wheelbase will have an advantage here. Front wheel drive cars have a tendency to have lower acceleration performance compared to other drivetrain layouts, so improving acceleration through gear ratios and other drivetrain tuning, and suspension settings for quick turning is recommended. As an example, setting the front suspension softer will improve turning performance of the car.

You can acquire this Mitsubishi VGT car just by participating in this event*. Get your hands on the next-generation hybrid concept car, developed with cutting edge technology! (* 1 full lap must be driven, regardless of whether the lap time was valid or not.)

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial Event using non racing versions of the high performance BMW M Series. The M series cars are powerful to begin with, so we recommend tuning the drive train and suspension rather than increasing power. It will help to set the car so that it can be swung around in a wide speed range from slow to high speeds. Try not to go too wide on the tight corners from section 1 to 3, and maintain your drift as long as possible in section 4 in order to gain the highest scores. Section 4 is not only long but is on an ascending slope, so power and speed will be key here. Try to clear the section at full throttle!

description.JP: This is a drift trial event using French non-racing cars. You'll find that many French cars are compact front engine front wheel drives, but we recommend finding a rear wheel drive as they are better suited for drifting. And city tracks tend to have narrow course width and the corners are tight. You will need to be careful in section 2 where you need to change direction, as it is easy to hit the walls here. Though it is best to maintain your drift while going through multiple corners, it is important to drive each corner carefully when you are first getting used to it. Use the wide course width at the third section to your advantage to aim for a high score.

And city tracks tend to have narrow course width and the corners are tight. You will need to be careful in section 2 where you need to change direction, as it is easy to hit the walls here. Though it is best to maintain your drift while going through multiple corners, it is important to drive each corner carefully when you are first getting used to it. Use the wide course width at the third section to your advantage to aim for a high score.

description.JP: This is a Time Trial event using a 1960's American car with 500PP or less. Muscle cars from this era have a powerful engine but the suspension and transmission are not very advanced. To improve lap times, you will need to tune the suspension and drivetrain, rather than just increasing power. You will probably require a full customizable transmission for the best results. If the car is leaning a lot in the corners the wheel on the inner side will tend to lift and lose traction, so installing an LSD will help to prevent this.

description.JP: TThis is a time trial event using non-racing, rear wheel drive cars with 450PP or less. There are 3 types of rear wheel drive cars, categorized by its engine mounting position. The front engine rear wheel drive (FR) with the engine mounted in front of the car, the mid engine rear wheel drive (MR) with the engine mounted behind the drivers seat, and the rear engine rear wheel drive (RR) with the engine mounted towards the rear of the car. Though they are all rear wheel drive, these have drastically different characteristics under extreme racing conditions, and you should choose a drivetrain that best suits you. It also depends on the car but as a general rule the FR is relatively straightforward, and while they are slightly more difficult to drive, MR and RR are fast if you have the skill to maximize their potential.

It also depends on the car but as a general rule the FR is relatively straightforward, and while they are slightly more difficult to drive, MR and RR are fast if you have the skill to maximize their potential.

Most drift sections on the Red Bull Ring will give you a better score if you enter slowly and accelerate out towards the exit. The first section is especially tight, so you should watch your entry speed.

description.JP: This is a Drift Trial event on the Brands Hatch Grand Prix Circuit '80s using distinctive (non-racing) cars from 1989 or earlier. Drift tuning for older cars depends heavily on suspension tuning. Many cars have a high centre of gravity and soft suspension, so you'll want to harden the suspension and lower the ride height until you find the best spot. The judged sections are mainly on the high speed corners, so high speed stability will have the most effect on your score. Choose your tires well to match your engine power.
